mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls >0.5% YoY and UNRATE exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of four consecutive months with PAYEMS > 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO declines of >0.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY) signals accommodative monetary policy, which lowers borrowing costs and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 months AND CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during episodes of prolonged low rates and low inflation as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase of more than 2% in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) coincident with a decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 6-month moving average signals a shift from housing to other consumer goods, which can boost retail and services sectors and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of GDPC1 YoY > 2% and HOUST below its 6-month moving average.
